The marriage certificate in the Lim Family Archive records Lim Ah Kow's spouse as Tan Bee Choo. Record status: current.

- Groom: Lim Ah Kow, son of Lim Ah Seng, of Singapore.
- Bride: Tan Bee Choo, daughter of Tan Cheng Lock, of Malacca.

- Place of marriage: No. 12 Arab Street, Singapore.
- Witnesses: Lim Ah Seng (father of groom), Tan Cheng Lock (father of bride).

ADDENDUM — MARRIAGE OF LIM AH KOW AND TAN BEE CHOO

The marriage certificate in the Lim Family Archive records Lim Ah Kow's spouse as Tan Bee Choo. Record status: current.

- Groom: Lim Ah Kow, son of Lim Ah Seng, of Singapore.
- Bride: Tan Bee Choo, daughter of Tan Cheng Lock, of Malacca.
- Date of marriage: 12 February 1875.
- Place of marriage: No. 12 Arab Street, Singapore.
- Witnesses: Lim Ah Seng (father of groom), Tan Cheng Lock (father of bride).

Remarks: This certificate is the authoritative record of the marriage. It has been compared with the entry in the marriage register (Volume 1, page 3), which matches in all particulars. The certificate is in good condition, though the edges are slightly frayed. This entry is current.

P2. "Group at the wedding of Lim Ah Kow & Tan Bee Choo." Studio portrait, sepia, mounted on card. Twelve people are pictured: the couple, both sets of parents, and eight other guests. Handwritten caption on the back: "Family and friends, 12 Feb 1875." Condition: fair, crease across the middle.

P3. "Lim Ah Kow & Tan Bee Choo, 25th anniversary, 12 Feb 1900." Studio portrait, sepia, mounted on card. The couple is seated with their children standing behind them.

**Memorandum of Association – Extracts**

(Registered 1 July 1905)

Clause 1. The name of the Company is CHENG TECK & SONS (SINGAPORE) PRIVATE LIMITED.

Clause 2. The registered office of the Company shall be situate in Singapore.

Clause 3. The objects for which the Company is established are:

(a) To carry on the business of merchants, importers, exporters, commission agents, and general dealers in all kinds of goods, wares, and merchandise.

(b) To acquire by purchase, lease, or otherwise any lands, buildings, hereditaments, and property of any kind whatsoever.

(c) To erect, maintain, and improve any buildings, wharves, godowns, and other works necessary or convenient for the purposes of the Company.

(d) To lend money to such persons or companies on such terms as may seem expedient.

(e) To invest and deal with the moneys of the Company not immediately required upon such securities as may be determined.

(f) To enter into partnership or into any arrangement for sharing profits, union of interests, co-operation, joint adventure, reciprocal concession, or otherwise with any person or company carrying on or engaged in any business or transaction which the Company is authorised to carry on.

Clause 4. The liability of the members is limited.

Clause 5. The capital of the Company is one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000), divided into one hundred shares of one thousand dollars ($1,000) each, with power to increase such capital.

---

**Articles of Association – Selected Provisions**

(Registered 1 July 1905)

Art. 18. The business of the Company shall be managed by the Directors, who may exercise all such powers of the Company as are not by the Ordinance or by these Articles required to be exercised by the Company in general meeting.

Art. 22. The quorum necessary for the transaction of the business of the Directors shall be two.

Art. 27. The Directors may from time to time appoint any person to be an attorney or agent of the Company for such purposes and with such powers, authorities, and discretions (not exceeding those vested in or exercisable by the Directors) as may be thought fit.
